versions.name: Camp Baldwin

features.note: Outbound trips beyond camp, including Class III whitewater on the Deschutes River and the Whitewater merit badge.
Trail rides for all sizes, plus the CL Advanced Wrangler program in which older Scouts work alongside the wranglers.
Forest trail riding, with advanced sessions covering trail skills and maintenance.
Advanced horse, biking, and boarding sessions built for older Scouts.
Jamboree-style cooking: campers cook half their meals in the campsite, with equipment, stoves, propane, and mess kits provided.
Rover Camp forms a provisional troop with its own staff leadership for Scouts attending without a troop.
Climbing on the natural faces of Vulture Rocks rather than a built tower.

versions.summary: Wooded resident camp in the Cascade foothills featuring a lake waterfront, dining hall, shooting sports, climbing, and COPE, with STEM offerings, a first-year Scout program, and an older Scout program.

sources.citation: Community correction via Camp Finder Suggest-a-Correction form; submitted by a unit that attended 2026-08-14 (submission Kpap8X7), kept anonymous at submitter request. Camp is on Mount Hood (the Dufur / east side), not in Sandy; the prior address and coordinates placed it on the west side near Sandy. Address and coordinates cleared pending re-geocoding, to be sourced from the council's Camp Baldwin page.

Coordinate set 2026-08-14 from the council's Camp Baldwin page (76201 Dufur Valley Rd, Dufur OR, on the east side of Mount Hood; the council's own stated coordinates); elevation from the open-meteo DEM. July normals still pending a WorldClim resample.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Website canonicalised 2026-07-25: https://cpcbsa.org/camping/camp-baldwin/ now redirects to https://cpcscouting.org/project/camp-baldwin/ (link audit, tools/check_urls.py). Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence). Unconfirmed codes inherited from camp-finder's frontend fixture data were removed 2026-07-27: camp-finder recorded these camps as fixture data for frontend development, not a live scrape, and no reachable source attests the removed codes. Generic amenities (dining hall, waterfront) are kept — this camp's page is a stub, so its silence about them is not evidence. Distinctive facilities a camp page would advertise are not.
